solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sluggish pig circling pound

indicators.note: the pig goes round the pound, so its letters enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A lazy pig plods around its pen, the pound where strays are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like an animal enclosure, which suits the pig, but it is the money abbreviation L.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sluggish moves with little speed or energy.

clue.text: Release brick-building toy around the end of August

indicators.note: the toy's name wraps round the final letter, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Lego is the famous plastic construction-brick toy

indicators.note: asks for only the final letter of the month's name

explanation.surface: A child is told to drop the Lego set once the summer holidays end in late August.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb synonym: to free one's grip on something or someone is to release it.

clue.text: Royal residence's type of chair by shed, extremely large

parts.note: a Windsor chair is a classic wooden chair with a spindle back
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: takes only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word large

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a palace's furniture: a chair set beside an outbuilding of great size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' reads as a garden hut but is the verb meaning cast off; the 's after residence is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the castle in Berkshire is one of the British monarch's official homes.

clue.text: Celebrity to start physical exercise

parts.note: a star is a famous person, a celebrity
to jump is to start suddenly in surprise

explanation.surface: A famous person is about to begin a fitness routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a leap with arms and legs spread wide is a common warm-up exercise, popular in PE lessons.

clue.text: Fanatic upside down in street, a daring feat

indicators.note: the overturned word sits inside the street abbreviation
in a down entry the word for a fanatic is turned over, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a fitness nut

explanation.surface: A wild enthusiast hanging upside down in the road is performing something risky.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stunt is a spectacular, risky act done to impress, like a stuntman's work.

clue.text: On front of stage amongst organised cast? She might be

indicators.note: the two small pieces go inside the rearranged letters
the letters of cast are put into a new order

parts.note: RE means on, concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: takes only the first letter of stage

explanation.surface: Asks whether a woman stepping to the front of the stage among a cast is one of the performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' shuffles the four letters of the cast to give ACTS. The question mark points back: the whole clue describes her, so 'She might be' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who performs in plays among a cast on stage could be described this way.

clue.text: Old US president? Press regularly sees cartoon character

parts.note: to jam is to press or squeeze, as in jamming things into a bag

indicators.note: takes every other letter of sees, here the second and fourth

parts.note: Garfield is the lasagne-loving cartoon cat

explanation.surface: Asks whether a former president is the one the newspapers keep spotting as a cartoon figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists but is the verb JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 20th American head of state, assassinated in 1881 after months in office.

clue.text: After short time, retailer reduced European wine

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a short time

indicators.note: the word for a retailer loses its final letter

parts.note: a seller is someone who retails goods

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper soon cuts the price of a continental wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a white wine from the valley of a river flowing through France, Luxembourg and Germany.

clue.text: Formal attire — tone altered with diamonds perhaps

indicators.note: the letters of tone are changed into a new order

parts.note: diamonds is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Formal dress given a new look with diamond jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a short-jacketed outfit once worn by boys at a famous English public school, now formal wear.

clue.text: Part of time-share network

indicators.note: the letters are a part of the phrase time-share, running across the hyphen

explanation.surface: Talks of a holiday time-share scheme belonging to a wider network.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a mesh is an interlaced net-like structure, a network of strands.

clue.text: Party run by group in English county

parts.note: a do is a party or social event
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
a set is a group of things or people

explanation.surface: A party organised by a club somewhere in rural England.
explanation.walkthrough: DORSET is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: one of England's southern shire counties, home of the Jurassic Coast.

clue.text: Assume complete, mostly

indicators.note: only most of the word is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: done means complete, finished

explanation.surface: Take it for granted that something is nearly finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assume' is meant in the sense of putting on clothes, not supposing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to don a hat or role is to put it on, to take it up.

clue.text: Savings account reviewed in cathedral city without a problem

indicators.note: the turned savings account goes inside the city

parts.note: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

indicators.note: the abbreviation is looked at again, read backwards

parts.note: an ISA is a British tax-free Individual Savings Account

explanation.surface: Someone's savings are checked in a cathedral city and pass without difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done easily means done with no difficulty at all.

clue.text: Unremarkable feature of earth tremor?

definitions.meaning: idiom for mediocre, not very good
a tremor is only a minor quake, so the shaking it brings is not big

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a minor earthquake is anything special.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something not much good is dismissed as of little account, ordinary.

clue.text: Having continued success, Jonah's content to wallow

indicators.note: what Jonah holds is his inside, the letters between his first and last

parts.note: the possessive reads as the name Jonah, whose contents are wanted
to roll about, as in mud, is to wallow

explanation.surface: Swallowed by the whale, Jonah is happy to wallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' looks like happy, but it is the noun: what is inside Jonah, his middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a streak of wins or good luck is described as being in a run of form.

clue.text: Large body of water abroad Alan found in different areas

indicators.note: the short name is placed inside the rearranged letters
the letters of areas are made different, rearranged

parts.note: Al is a short form of the name Alan

explanation.surface: A man called Alan travels overseas, turning up in various regions by a big lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shrinking inland lake in Central Asia, between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

clue.text: View bishop's office

definitions.meaning: a diocese, the seat and jurisdiction of a bishop

explanation.surface: Pay a visit to the bishop's office.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym and church sense: watch, and the area a bishop governs, as in the Holy one in Rome.

clue.text: Fruit seaman knocked back with Charlie

indicators.note: the sailor's abbreviation is sent backwards

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
a charlie and a nana are both British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: A sailor is fed fruit while downing drinks with his friend Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a 'right Charlie' or a 'nana' is a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long yellow tropical fruit, a common breakfast item.

clue.text: Wife and two females, consumed by beer, talk gibberish

indicators.note: the pair of letters is swallowed inside the beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them give a pair

explanation.surface: A wife and two women drink beer and start talking nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to waffle is to ramble on at length without saying much of sense.

clue.text: Produce literary work fit to broadcast

indicators.note: the word is heard over the air, so it is spelt differently but pronounced the same

parts.note: right means fit or proper, as in fit and right for the job

explanation.surface: Create a literary work suitable for radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an author composes books or poems, putting words on paper.

clue.text: Half-finished lips lacked colour

indicators.note: each word is cut off halfway, keeping only its first half

explanation.surface: Lipstick only half applied left the lips without colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of LIPS is LI and half of LACKED is LAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a pale purple shade, named after the flowering shrub.

clue.text: One who entertains son during baking

indicators.note: the son is placed within the word for baking, as if in the middle of it

parts.note: baking hot weather is very hot
S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone hosting guests while their son is busy in the kitchen with cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baking' suggests the oven but means very hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a person who receives guests at home or at a party.

clue.text: Rogue pipe reportedly transmitted disease

parts.note: a swine is a contemptible person, a rogue

indicators.note: as spoken, the chimney pipe word gives a shorter spelling

parts.note: a flue is a pipe or duct for smoke

explanation.surface: A villain's pipe is said to have spread an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like an anagram signal but is the synonym SWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a strain of influenza that passed from pigs to people, spreading worldwide in 2009.

clue.text: Lose the friendship of Natalie, moving east

indicators.note: the letters of Natalie are moved about into a new order

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Natalie's move to the east costs her a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to alienate someone is to turn them against you, estranging them.

clue.text: Fish salsa, for example, not new

indicators.note: the abbreviation for new is excluded from the word

parts.note: the salsa is a Latin American dance

explanation.surface: A fish dish with salsa, but not a fresh one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salsa' suggests a sauce served with fish; it is the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small freshwater fish of the carp family found in European rivers.
